guide.mmcr_patchouli.name: Modular Machinery Guide
guide.mmcr_patchouli.landing: This guide introduces some of Modular Machinery's core features and selected addon content.$(br2)Modular Machinery itself does not provide any preconfigured machines. Actual machines are supplied by modpacks or addons; whether a component is valid depends on the modpack or addon's configuration.

guide.mmcr_patchouli.entry.basics.overvi: A modular machine typically consists of a controller, structural blocks, and functional components.$(br2)The controller recognizes the structure and manages operation; input ports supply recipe inputs (such as materials and energy), while output ports collect recipe products. Machine casings make up the machine's structure.$(br2)Every machine has a $(l:mmcr:controllers/controller)controller$(/l).

Specific machines are supplied by modpacks or addons. If neither provides custom machine content, no machine controllers will be available in game (though this guide remains readable).$(br2)Special interfaces are only meaningful when supported by the corresponding machine. In an unsupported machine structure, they may not be recognized as part of the structure or may be unable to function.
guide.mmcr_patchouli.entry.basics.acquis: A Modular Machinery Guide can be crafted shapelessly using an ordinary book and a Modularium Ingot. The ingredients can be placed in any positions.$(br2)Without Patchouli, neither this book nor its recipe is provided.
Modularium Ingots are this mod's basic crafting material, unless the recipes have been customized.
guide.mmcr_patchouli.entry.basics.casing: The basic casing is a decorative block provided by MMCR. Apart from being a basic crafting material for ports, it has no special function.
guide.mmcr_patchouli.entry.controllers.c: The machine controller is the core block of a machine. Each machine's controller is registered dynamically with its machine content.

Placement facing determines the orientation of the entire structure. Machines that only support horizontal facing cannot be placed vertically; machines that support vertical facing can face up or down depending on the placement face and player position.$(br2)After placing the controller, use a $(l:mmcr:tools/blueprint)blueprint$(/l) or $(l:mmcr:tools/terminal)terminal$(/l) to check details such as the structure's orientation.

The $(l:mmcr:processing/factory)factory controller$(/l) is a scheduling component that can be added to supported structures; it cannot replace the machine's original controller.$(br2)Once a factory controller is recognized, the machine's entry point displays the factory thread screen, while the factory controller's own screen is used to insert thread-capacity items.
guide.mmcr_patchouli.entry.controllers.f: Right-click the controller to open the machine screen. Every type of machine screen has a structure-check button.$(br2)To check an unformed machine, keep both hands empty and sneak-right-click the controller. This sends a structure preview and immediately requests a check.$(br2)You can also use the $(l:mmcr:tools/terminal)terminal's check function$(/l).

Use the preview to verify block types, states, positions, and counts. Port direction (input/output), family, and tier may also affect whether the machine forms. A higher-capacity port is not necessarily a valid substitute for the specified port block during formation.$(br2)For multi-stage structures, view the correct structure stage.

Shared components must follow the sharing restrictions declared by the machine. Ports shared by two overlapping structures may not be able to serve both machines simultaneously; parallel controllers are another example.$(br2)It is best to keep the structure's chunks loaded (this does not cause excessive performance overhead and is much more reasonable than loading only the controller's chunk).
guide.mmcr_patchouli.entry.controllers.o: Formed does not mean running.$(br2)Read status, recipe, and progress. Idle, no recipe, insufficient resources, and paused are different states. During operation, product and energy information reflects the current recipe and actual parallelism.

Machines only select recipes from their available recipe pools.$(br2)Machine level and structure stage are different: the former comes from conditions such as level slots, while the latter describes a phase of the whole structure. Some recipes may require both.
A direct redstone signal pauses the controller.$(br2)Do not judge whether the machine is working by appearance alone. See $(l:mmcr:troubleshooting/common)troubleshooting$(/l).
guide.mmcr_patchouli.entry.ports.items.p: Input buses hold items for recipes to consume. Right-click to open the screen and insert materials, or supply them by other means, such as pipes. They support automatic input and output.
Output buses receive machine products. Leave compatible space available for those items.

Normal bus tiers provide different slot layouts; $(l:mmcr:ports/extended_items)extended item buses$(/l) focus on bulk item storage, and the screen displays actual quantities.$(br2)To automatically supply materials or eject products, select the resource type and configure the direction on the $(l:mmcr:ports/auto_io)auto IO page$(/l).
Fluid input hatches supply fluids to machines. Use fluid containers to manually insert or extract, or connect pipes to supply fluids. See the container controls on a later page.
Fluid output hatches receive fluid products for removal by containers or transport equipment. Incompatible contents or insufficient free space can block output.

For bulk fluid storage, see $(l:mmcr:ports/extended_fluids)extended fluid hatches$(/l).$(br2)Insufficient input and insufficient output space are separate problems. Chemicals cannot be stored here as ordinary fluids!
guide.mmcr_patchouli.container_interacti: Container controls for normal hatches and normal combined ports:$(br2)GUI: hold a supported container on the cursor. Left-click a tank to insert into an input hatch; Shift-left-click to extract. Output hatches only extract with either click.$(br2)World: right-click without sneaking while holding a container to extract first. Only if this fails completely will input hatches try insertion. Pipe IO directions remain unchanged.
Energy input hatches store energy for machines to consume. External cables can be used for energy input and output. Insufficient stored energy can affect recipe operation.
Energy output hatches receive energy generated by recipes and transfer it outside the machine.

$(l:mmcr:ports/extended_energy)Extended energy hatches$(/l) offer greater capacity and transfer rates.$(br2)For unstable operation, check stored energy, the power source, and $(l:mmcr:ports/auto_io)auto IO$(/l).
guide.mmcr_patchouli.entry.ports.combine: A combined input port provides item and fluid inputs in one block. Each resource has separate storage and auto-IO settings. GUI container actions affect only the clicked fluid tank.
A combined output port receives both item and fluid products. Both sides need free space, and blockage on either side can affect the entire recipe.
$(l:mmcr:ports/extended_combined)Extended combined ports$(/l) provide bulk item and fluid storage.$(br2)Configure items and fluids separately on the $(l:mmcr:ports/auto_io)auto IO page$(/l).
guide.mmcr_patchouli.entry.ports.auto_io: Right-click a port that supports auto IO, then use the page-switch button to open its controls. Multi-resource ports let you select items, fluids, and other resource types separately.$(br2)Input ports pull from adjacent storage; output ports push to adjacent receivers. Master and side switches apply to the selected resource type.

Click the six face buttons to toggle automatic transfer for each face. The buttons can show adjacent blocks.$(br2)Turning off the master switch stops automatic transfer even on enabled faces. Neighbors must support the resource and allow extraction or insertion in the required direction.

Eject Contents on an input port tries to return the selected resource to adjacent receivers. Click for the first resource kind; Shift-click to request all kinds.$(br2)Ports used by active recipes cannot eject. Without a receiver, contents stay inside. Output ports do not have this button.
guide.mmcr_patchouli.entry.processing.pa: Parallel controllers increase the batch-processing limit per recipe for machines that support them. Different tiers offer different levels of support, and the actual effect also depends on the machine's parallelism cap and recipe settings.

Parallelism means processing multiple copies of the same recipe at once.$(br2)Actual parallelism is limited by ingredient quantities, output space, energy, and machine conditions; raising the cap does not mean it will always be reached. Check $(l:mmcr:ports/items)item$(/l), $(l:mmcr:ports/fluids)fluid$(/l), and $(l:mmcr:ports/energy)energy$(/l) supplies.
guide.mmcr_patchouli.entry.processing.fa: The factory controller is a multithreaded scheduling component. When placed in a permitted structure position, it allows machines that support factory mode to schedule multiple recipe threads.

The machine controller's factory screen shows each thread's status and progress. Factory threads run recipes independently; $(l:mmcr:processing/parallel)parallelism$(/l) batches work within one thread.$(br2)$(l:mmcr:processing/thread_disperser)Thread Rippers$(/l) add scheduling capacity. Machine limits, recipe thread caps, and shared input/output resources still limit actual operation.
guide.mmcr_patchouli.entry.processing.th: Place Thread Rippers in the factory controller's dedicated item slot.

Slot contents contribute to thread capacity; changes update the linked factory.$(br2)This is not a CPU setting or a guarantee of one running recipe per item. Check $(l:mmcr:processing/factory)factory support$(/l), resources, and recipe thread limits first.
guide.mmcr_patchouli.entry.components.up: Upgrade buses hold upgrade items supported by the machine. Bus families offer different slot counts.

Insert the upgrades specified by the machine's instructions. They may affect operating conditions or processing capabilities; types and stacking rules depend on the machine and upgrade definitions.$(br2)If they have no effect, check structure recognition and item support first. Do not treat ordinary materials or thread-capacity items as universal upgrades!
guide.mmcr_patchouli.entry.components.sm: Smart interfaces provide editable numeric parameters for a linked machine. Available types come from that machine. Without a valid binding or defined parameters, there is nothing to edit.

Right-click to open the screen, select a parameter, and read its description and current value. Enter a number, then click Save or press Enter; integer parameters do not accept fractions.$(br2)Values may affect recipe conditions or machine effects, as defined by the machine.
guide.mmcr_patchouli.entry.components.da: Data storage holds a linked machine's runtime data and provides no ordinary item input/output. Use it only when needed by the machine's structure and behavior.
Data storage links to at most one controller. The machine can save and read its data. Whether it appears in the machine screen and how it affects operation depend on the machine.
guide.mmcr_patchouli.entry.components.mo: A module bridge connects a supported host and module. Both structures must use the same bridge at valid positions, and the host must allow that module type.

Check that both the host and module are formed, then check whether the module is connected to the host. A formed but offline module may still be unable to run.$(br2)The bridge position must uniquely correspond to a valid host and module. Overlapping shared functional interfaces can cause conflicts. If connection fails, check allowed types, structures, and bridge positions. Do not simply place a module next to the host!
guide.mmcr_patchouli.entry.tools.bluepri: Sneak-right-click a machine controller while holding a blueprint to bind its machine. Then hold the blueprint in your main hand and right-click the air to open the structure preview.

Plus/minus buttons select display layers; A shows all layers and R resets the view. Multi-stage machines also have previous/next stage buttons.$(br2)A layer is a viewing slice along the Y axis; a structure stage is a phase of the whole structure. Click preview blocks for allowed replacements. The material list reflects the current preview.

The tooltip's material list uses the lowest structure stage and default-level blocks; hold Shift to expand it.$(br2)When building, check the screen's structure stage and replacement options. Use a $(l:mmcr:tools/terminal)terminal$(/l) to select a specific building level. Blueprints do not place blocks automatically.
guide.mmcr_patchouli.entry.tools.termina: Main-hand sneak-right-click binds a controller. Air right-click opens the screen; sneak-use in air unbinds the controller and resets structure selections and preview. Stay within operating distance.

Inventory mode uses your materials. Select container mode in the screen, then sneak-right-click a valid container to bind it. Clear keeps the inventory mode, container binding, and wireless access point binding.$(br2)Choose the structure stage and machine level, then use Preview, display layers, and Check to verify the target. See $(l:mmcr:controllers/formation)formation checks$(/l).

Build takes materials from the selected inventory and places blocks allowed by the machine.$(br2)Demolish targets the selected structure and returns recoverable items to the selected inventory. Leave room for returned items.

Keep the terminal in your main hand during operation. The controller must be in the same dimension and within the server-configured operating radius; target chunks must also be loaded.$(br2)Unavailable containers or other inventories prevent building and demolition. Preview only shows the target. Follow the status messages to check binding, distance, and materials.
guide.mmcr_patchouli.entry.tools.export_: A developer tool available only in creative mode.$(br2)The multiblock export tool marks regions for structure creation and export. Right-click a block for the first corner; sneak-right-click for the second. While holding the tool, use Pick Block to mark the controller position and face.
Hold the tool in your main hand and right-click the air to open settings; sneak-use in the air to clear the selection. The tooltip lists recorded positions.
guide.mmcr_patchouli.entry.network.inter: A network interface is a machine-network endpoint that must be recognized by a valid formed machine. It is not an AE2 ME interface, and connecting a cable does not make it an ME storage port.

Connections need machine support, allowed endpoint types, free connection capacity, and valid machine states.$(br2)Use a $(l:mmcr:network/key_card)key card$(/l) to select source and target. Adding an interface does not give every machine new network features.
guide.mmcr_patchouli.entry.network.key_c: Sneak-right-click a valid network interface to select the source endpoint. Normally right-click the target interface to attempt a connection. Sneak-use in the air to clear the card's selection.

The selected source interface must belong to a valid formed machine. An invalid source machine or interface, invalid target, disallowed type, or full connection capacity rejects the connection with a message.$(br2)If it fails, check the $(l:mmcr:network/interfaces)network interface conditions$(/l) and reselect the source if needed.
guide.mmcr_patchouli.entry.troubleshooti: $(bold)Structure first$(reset)$(br)Check facing, blocks, port tiers, stage, and loaded chunks with $(l:mmcr:controllers/formation)formation checks$(/l).$(br2)Then verify the recipe pool, machine level, and structure stage support the target recipe.

$(bold)Resources next$(reset)$(br)Put materials in $(l:mmcr:ports/items)input buses$(/l) or the correct fluid inputs. Maintain enough $(l:mmcr:ports/energy)energy$(/l) and compatible output space.$(br2)Check $(l:mmcr:ports/auto_io)auto IO$(/l): resource type, master switch, faces, and adjacent storage. Higher parallelism needs more materials and output space.

$(bold)Extra conditions$(reset)$(br)Remove pausing redstone signals. Check $(l:mmcr:components/modules)module connections$(/l) and $(l:mmcr:components/smart_interface)parameters$(/l) when required.$(br2)Factory capacity is not the number of active threads. An offline interface network does not indicate a missing structure.
Connect to an ME network and configure items or fluids in the interface screen. Normal input interfaces first pull materials into their own storage; the machine consumes this local inventory.

Meet machine structure rules and ME network conditions. Check actual interface contents, not just stocking targets.$(br2)A configured target is not owned material. For direct network-stock consumption, see $(l:mmcr:ae2/me_stocking_input)stocking inputs$(/l).
guide.mmcr_patchouli.entry.ae2.me_stocki: Configure the item or fluid types the machine may use. Stocking inputs consume ME network inventory directly, and displayed storage amounts mirror network stock rather than a separate local cache in the block.

Unlike $(l:mmcr:ae2/me_input)normal inputs$(/l), no local stock accumulates. Recipes extract configured types from ME, and configured quantities do not create additional inventory.$(br2)Keep the network usable and stocked. Disconnection or consumption by other devices changes displayed and actually available amounts.
guide.mmcr_patchouli.entry.ae2.me_output: Send machine items and fluids into the ME network. Normal output interfaces have a bounded local cache; network scheduling continues moving cached products into storage.

An offline network, missing compatible storage, or insufficient space prevents the cache from draining. A full cache then blocks machine output.$(br2)Check network power, connectivity, and storage space. $(l:mmcr:ae2/me_async_output)Async outputs$(/l) buffer differently.
guide.mmcr_patchouli.entry.ae2.me_async_: Async outputs receive products in a temporary in-memory queue, then send batches through ME network scheduling. They do not use the normal output's persisted local cache and have no offline-storage fallback.

Unloading a chunk, removing the block, or deactivating the network node clears any queued outputs that have not yet been delivered (this penalty directly causes output loss, so make sure the network remains operational). Keep the network and chunks available while in use.$(br2)Async means neither unlimited capacity nor guaranteed speed over normal ME output interfaces. Acceptance still depends on available network insertion space. For local caching, see $(l:mmcr:ae2/me_output)normal output interfaces$(/l).
guide.mmcr_patchouli.entry.ae2.me_patter: Insert processing patterns matching machine recipes and connect the interface to an ME network. It coordinates AE2 autocrafting requests with linked machines, enabling more advanced logistics-based crafting.

The machine must be formed and operational, with a recipe and resources that satisfy the request.$(br2)Finished products enter the pattern provider's return inventory and are then returned to the network by AE2's native return logic to complete the craft. If the network cannot accept them, resolve the return blockage first.

The pattern interface screen provides settings such as patterns and blocking mode; these settings determine when a request can proceed.$(br2)When adjusting multitasking capacity, first distinguish between $(l:mmcr:processing/factory)factory threads$(/l) and $(l:mmcr:processing/parallel)per-recipe parallelism$(/l).
guide.mmcr_patchouli.entry.ae2.terminal_: Open an AE2 wireless access point and place the terminal in its linking input slot, then take it from the output slot. Binding only updates the ME connection; other settings stay unchanged. Select ME inventory mode in the terminal to use the network. Bind the machine controller separately.

The wireless access point must be loaded and active, and connected to a network with inventory. Building extracts structure materials from that network, while demolition returns recoverable items to it.$(br2)ME inventory mode does not remove the controller's same-dimension and operating-distance restrictions. If materials are insufficient, the network is unavailable, or items cannot be returned, demolition is aborted. For basic operations, see the $(l:mmcr:tools/terminal)terminal$(/l).
guide.mmcr_patchouli.entry.extendedae.in: Extended input interfaces provide more configuration and storage slots, with four times as many usable slots as a normal ME interface.
Extended stocking input interfaces retain $(l:mmcr:ae2/me_stocking_input)direct network inventory consumption$(/l) and likewise have four times as many slots as a normal ME interface.
Extended output interfaces provide more configuration and storage slots, with four times as many usable slots as a normal ME interface.
Oversize input interfaces are upgraded versions of extended input interfaces, offering more slots as well as greater storage capacity per slot.
Oversize output interfaces are upgraded versions of extended output interfaces, offering more slots as well as greater storage capacity per slot.
Extended pattern interfaces provide more pattern slots and use the same $(l:mmcr:ae2/me_pattern)pattern request and product return$(/l) process.
For stocking input interfaces, per-slot storage capacity is irrelevant. Extended stocking input interfaces provide more slots.
guide.mmcr_patchouli.entry.appflux.flux_: ME flux input interfaces supply machines from AppliedFlux's ME energy storage. They need a working network, extractable energy, and machine support for this input component.

ME flux output interfaces send generated energy into AppliedFlux network storage. Insufficient acceptance space affects output. Input and output are not interchangeable; see $(l:mmcr:ports/energy)energy direction and supply$(/l).
guide.mmcr_patchouli.entry.mekanism.chem: Chemical input hatches supply Mekanism chemicals. Chemicals differ from ordinary fluids; fluid input hatches are not substitutes. Normal chemical hatches accept only non-radioactive chemicals.
Chemical output hatches receive non-radioactive chemical products for removal by chemical transport equipment.

Hatches from Basic to higher tiers provide different storage capacities and may be used to satisfy machine port-tier requirements. Radioactive materials require $(l:mmcr:mekanism/radioactivity)dedicated radioactive hatches$(/l).
guide.mmcr_patchouli.entry.mekanism.radi: Radioactive input hatches accept only chemicals with the radioactive property, for machine consumption. Normal chemical hatches reject these resources.
Radioactive output hatches receive radioactive chemical products. Extract them with a receiver supporting the resource, and confirm that the structure allows this component.

Radioactive hatches are storage ports restricted by chemical type. They do not purify, remove radiation, or process waste.$(br2)When a hatch is removed, radiation release logic is invoked for its contents if Mekanism radiation is enabled. Handle the contents through valid transport before dismantling.
guide.mmcr_patchouli.entry.mekanism.heat: Heat input hatches accept incoming external heat to satisfy machine heat or minimum-temperature conditions.
Heat output hatches receive heat generated by the machine and transfer it to supported adjacent equipment. Output hatches do not accept incoming external heat.

Heat is stored energy; temperature describes thermal state; heat capacity determines temperature changes for a given amount of heat.$(br2)Heat hatches lose heat to cooler surroundings, so temperature may drop when heating stops. Check heat and temperature readings, connected faces, and recipe conditions.
guide.mmcr_patchouli.entry.ports.extende: Extended Item Buses
Basic Input
The Basic extended item input bus provides 8 bulk storage positions for recipe materials.
Basic Output
The Basic extended item output bus has 8 bulk storage positions for machine products.
Advanced Input
The Advanced extended item input bus provides 16 bulk storage positions for recipe materials.
Advanced Output
The Advanced extended item output bus provides 16 bulk storage positions for machine products.
Reinforced In
The Reinforced extended item input bus provides 24 bulk storage positions for recipe materials.
Reinforced Out
The Reinforced extended item output bus provides 24 bulk storage positions for machine products.
Ultimate Input
The Ultimate extended item input bus has 32 bulk storage positions, the largest layout in this family.
Ultimate Output
The Ultimate extended item output bus provides 32 bulk storage positions, the largest layout in this family.

All four tiers use bulk storage at each position; upgrading increases the number of positions. The actual amounts shown in the interface are not the same as ordinary item stack display counts.$(br2)Use $(l:mmcr:ports/auto_io)auto IO$(/l) to supply or remove items.
Extended Fluid Hatches
Basic Input
The Basic extended fluid input hatch provides 8 bulk fluid storage positions.
Basic Output
The Basic extended fluid output hatch provides 8 bulk fluid storage positions.
Advanced Input
The Advanced extended fluid input hatch provides 16 bulk fluid storage positions.
Advanced Output
The Advanced extended fluid output hatch has 16 bulk fluid storage positions.
Reinforced In
The Reinforced extended fluid input hatch provides 24 bulk fluid storage positions.
Reinforced Out
The Reinforced extended fluid output hatch has 24 bulk fluid storage positions.
Ultimate Input
The Ultimate extended fluid input hatch has 32 bulk fluid storage positions, the largest layout in this family.
Ultimate Output
The Ultimate extended fluid output hatch provides 32 bulk fluid storage positions, the largest layout in this family.
The four tiers provide 8, 16, 24, and 32 fluid storage positions respectively, each using bulk storage.
Extended Energy Hatches
Reinforced In
Provides up to 2.1G of energy storage, with both storage capacity and input rate reaching the Integer.MAX_VALUE limit.
Reinforced Out
Provides up to 2.1G of energy storage, with both storage capacity and output rate reaching the Integer.MAX_VALUE limit.
Ultimate Input
Provides up to 9.2E of energy storage, with an input rate reaching the Integer.MAX_VALUE limit.
Ultimate Output
Provides up to 9.2E of energy storage, with an output rate reaching the Integer.MAX_VALUE limit.
This family includes Reinforced and Ultimate tiers, each available in input and output versions. Their rates reach the maximum permitted by gameplay limits.
Extended Combined Ports
Advanced Input
The Advanced extended combined input port supplies items and fluids from one block. It provides 6 item positions and 2 fluid positions, each using bulk storage.
Advanced Output
The Advanced extended combined output port receives both product types. It provides 6 item positions and 2 fluid positions, each using bulk storage.
Reinforced In
Provides 12 item positions and 4 fluid positions, each using bulk storage.
Reinforced Out
Provides 12 item positions and 4 fluid positions, each using bulk storage.
Ultimate Input
Provides 18 item positions and 6 fluid positions, the largest layout in this family.
Ultimate Output
Provides 18 item positions and 6 fluid positions, the largest layout in this family.
All three tiers of combined ports use bulk item and fluid storage.
